featured_reviews.name: Loyson Louis
featured_reviews.review_text:
Baba Falooda – Sitladevi Mandir Metro (Personal Review)
Rating: 2.5–3/5
What I liked:
Rich and generous faloodas loaded with rose syrup, sabja seeds, ice cream, kulfi pieces, and other toppings.
Fresh juices are decent.
The staff appear to make a sincere effort to maintain cleanliness despite being a roadside outlet.
Convenient if you're in the area and craving something cold and sweet.
What I didn't like:
No seating at all; everything is standing-room only.
Being a roadside stall, the entire preparation and serving area is exposed to traffic, dust, and pedestrians.
Presentation is basic—ingredients are packed into the glass without much finesse, and you practically have to "excavate" your falooda with a plastic spoon.
Prices are on the higher side (around ₹100+ per serving).
The constant presence of beggars approaching customers while they're eating can make the experience uncomfortable, especially when dining with a group.
Better alternatives nearby:
Badshah – Better ambience, seating, air-conditioned comfort, and a more enjoyable overall experience for falooda and cold beverages.
Gupta Kulfi Centre – Located opposite Baba Falooda, with air-conditioning and a more comfortable environment, even though space is limited.
Verdict: If you're thirsty and happen to be passing by, Baba Falooda can satisfy a craving for a rich, heavily loaded falooda. However, if comfort, ambience, presentation, and a relaxed experience matter to you, I'd personally choose Badshah ( Crawford market ) or the nearby Gupta Kulfi Centre instead.
"Good in an emergency, but not a destination I'd specifically visit for a falooda."

featured_reviews.name: Alfie Fernandes
featured_reviews.review_text: Tried the falooda based on the reviews, it was tasty, full of ice-cream blocks, generous milky syrup, priced well, it seems it gets very crowded in the evening, but when I saw the way ice-cream blocks were cut without any gloves and on cardboard covers, lacked basic hygiene, it was closed to the shewarna grill, not sure if meat and ice cream are stored in the same freezer, but that's what you get in Mumbai street food, full of flavours but be missing hygiene

featured_reviews.name: PD
featured_reviews.review_text:
I will let you in on a secret, whenever your partner is angry with you, take home a bowl of the rich goodness...the kulfi Rabdi bowl.... guarantee heart melting stuff ...can get you out of any kind of trouble
Baba Falooda’s special Malai Kulfi with Rabdi is pure indulgence. The kulfi is dense, creamy, and perfectly set — rich without being overly sweet — and the rabdi layered on top is thick, luscious, and full of that slow-cooked, caramelized milk flavor that feels nostalgic and comforting.
Every spoonful tastes premium and freshly prepared. The portion size is generous, the quality is consistent, and the balance of sweetness is just right. Whether you’re celebrating, apologizing, or simply craving something decadent, this bowl delivers every single time.
If you love traditional Indian desserts done right, Baba Falooda’s Malai Kulfi Rabdi is a must-try. Absolute heart-melting goodness.

featured_reviews.review_text:

From classic falooda to loaded ice-cream combinations, everything was delicious and served in generous portions. It’s definitely a paradise for dessert lovers.
Great place to visit with family or friends if you want to try multiple flavors and enjoy a sweet treat together. Highly recommended for anyone who loves ice-cream and falooda! 🍧

featured_reviews.name: Vinayak Londhe
featured_reviews.review_text:
Chotu’s Gola & Milkshake, 5 Gardens, Wadala

I recently visited Chotu’s Gola & Milkshake at 5 Gardens, Wadala, and it turned out to be a refreshing stop during my visit. I tried their Kala Khatta Gola, and I must say it was absolutely fantastic—full of flavor, tangy, and exactly the kind of taste you expect from a perfect gola. The ice was crushed well, the syrup was balanced, and overall it was very refreshing.

The only downside is that it feels slightly overpriced, as one Kala Khatta Gola costs ₹50, which is higher than usual street gola rates. However, considering that 5 Gardens doesn’t have many food stalls or shops around, the pricing may be influenced by the location.

The shop offers a good variety of flavours, not just in golas but also in milkshakes, mojitos, and other drinks. So whether you want something icy, creamy, or refreshing, there are multiple choices available. The stall is situated between the sandwich stall and the pani puri stall, making it easy to spot if you’re walking around 5 Gardens.

Chotu’s Gola & Milkshake usually opens around 3 PM and stays open till approximately 9 PM, which works perfectly for evening strolls or casual meetups in the garden area.

Overall, my experience was good—the gola was tasty, the flavors were strong, and it was perfect for the evening. If you’re in 5 Gardens, Wadala, and craving something refreshing, Chotu’s is definitely worth a try.

featured_reviews.name: Omkar Verma (ShotsbyOmkar)
featured_reviews.review_text:
Messy Addaa 2.0 in Matunga is a leafy, cozy café with a lush front yard and intimate backyard that sets the perfect relaxed, board-game vibe ﹣ ideal for casual catch-ups. We sampled a creative array of dishes:
1. Tandoori millet bowl was a light, nutritious starter.
2. Veggie Maggi lived up to its comfort-food reputation with inventive twists that Messy Addaa is known for !!
3. Black‑rice arancini delivered a delightful contrast of crunchy exterior and soft, cheesy-veg center.
4. Schezwan and Korean momos packed spicy punch and reinforced their status on Mumbai’s top dumpling list .
5. European sizzler, was again super good in taste. The creamy garlic gravy made the whole dish yummy.

For drinks, the Chilli Guava Cooler was refreshingly fruity with just the right kick, while the Cappuccino was smooth and reliably well-prepared, echoing positive reviews about their drinks and coffee .

Staff were generally friendly and polite😊.
The fusion-forward menu, greenery, and youthful ambiance make it a fun destination.❤️Overall, Messy Addaa 2.0 earns a 4.0/5 a green oasis for experimental bites and casual hangs, provided you manage expectations around service and portion size.
